content:
Hey everyone! My name is Bernie and I did my master's in representation theory where I was introduced to the wonderful world of birdtracks. For the many who have not heard of them, they're a graphical way to do some pretty neat tensor algebra. But, they're not very practically usable for real computations unless you like your number of terms exploding as multiples of factorials. There are many identities one can use to make computations actually feasible, but none have so far been implemented in a reliable way.

Over the past months, I've been working, with AI assistance, on a python implementation of birdtrack algebra and using that to write a (still pretty messy) algorithmic solver, with a graphical drawing front-end where users can actually physically construct birdtrack operators, multiply them, expand them, etc. My solver was getting to the point where I was wondering how I was ever going to be able to guarantee this thing was sound and correct in all instances. I started looking into how mathematical statements were computationally formalised in the broader community, and that's when I found Lean. I've been learning to use it and I like what I see, from the little I've seen so far.

I'm looking forward to learning more, so I wanted to introduce myself, take a look at what people here work on, and see if there were any folks here interested in what I've been up to.
